title: Clockwise/Spiral Rule
excerpt: There is a technique known as the ``Clockwise/Spiral Rule'' which enables any C programmer to parse in their head any C declaration!
content_html:
[This was posted to comp.lang.c by its author, David Anderson, on 1994-05-06.]

By David Anderson

There is a technique known as the ``Clockwise/Spiral Rule'' which enables any C programmer to parse in their head any C declaration!

There are three simple steps to follow:

  1. Starting with the unknown element, move in a spiral/clockwise direction; when ecountering the following elements replace them with the corresponding english statements:
    [X] or []
    => Array X size of... or Array undefined size of...
    (type1, type2)
    => function passing type1 and type2 returning...
    *
    => pointer(s) to...

  2. Keep doing this in a spiral/clockwise direction until all tokens have been covered.

  3. Always resolve anything in parenthesis first!

Example #1: Simple declaration

                     +-------+
                     | +-+   |
                     | ^ |   |
                char *str[10];
                 ^   ^   |   |
                 |   +---+   |
                 +-----------+
Question we ask ourselves: What is str?
``str is an...
  • We move in a spiral clockwise direction starting with `str' and the first character we see is a `[' so, that means we have an array, so...
    ``str is an array 10 of...
  • Continue in a spiral clockwise direction, and the next thing we encounter is the `*' so, that means we have pointers, so...
    ``str is an array 10 of pointers to...
  • Continue in a spiral direction and we see the end of the line (the `;'), so keep going and we get to the type `char', so...
    ``str is an array 10 of pointers to char''
  • We have now ``visited'' every token; therefore we are done!

Example #2: Pointer to Function declaration

                     +--------------------+
                     | +---+              |
                     | |+-+|              |
                     | |^ ||              |
                char *(*fp)( int, float *);
                 ^   ^ ^  ||              |
                 |   | +--+|              |
                 |   +-----+              |
                 +------------------------+
Question we ask ourselves: What is fp?
``fp is a...
  • Moving in a spiral clockwise direction, the first thing we see is a `)'; therefore, fp is inside parenthesis, so we continue the spiral inside the parenthesis and the next character seen is the `*', so...
    ``fp is a pointer to...
  • We are now out of the parenthesis and continuing in a spiral clockwise direction, we see the `('; therefore, we have a function, so...
    ``fp is a pointer to a function passing an int and a pointer to float returning...
  • Continuing in a spiral fashion, we then see the `*' character, so...
    ``fp is a pointer to a function passing an int and a pointer to float returning a pointer to...
  • Continuing in a spiral fashion we see the `;', but we haven't visited all tokens, so we continue and finally get to the type `char', so...
    ``fp is a pointer to a function passing an int and a pointer to float returning a pointer to a char''

Example #3: The ``Ultimate''

                      +-----------------------------+
                      |                  +---+      |
                      |  +---+           |+-+|      |
                      |  ^   |           |^ ||      |
                void (*signal(int, void (*fp)(int)))(int);
                 ^    ^      |      ^    ^  ||      |
                 |    +------+      |    +--+|      |
                 |                  +--------+      |
                 +----------------------------------+

Question we ask ourselves: What is `signal'?

Notice that signal is inside parenthesis, so we must resolve this first!

  • Moving in a clockwise direction we see `(' so we have...
    ``signal is a function passing an int and a...
  • Hmmm, we can use this same rule on `fp', so... What is fp? fp is also inside parenthesis so continuing we see an `*', so...
    fp is a pointer to...
  • Continue in a spiral clockwise direction and we get to `(', so...
    ``fp is a pointer to a function passing int returning...''
  • Now we continue out of the function parenthesis and we see void, so...
    ``fp is a pointer to a function passing int returning nothing (void)''
  • We have finished with fp so let's catch up with `signal', we now have...
    ``signal is a function passing an int and a pointer to a function passing an int returning nothing (void) returning...
  • We are still inside parenthesis so the next character seen is a `*', so...
    ``signal is a function passing an int and a pointer to a function passing an int returning nothing (void) returning a pointer to...
  • We have now resolved the items within parenthesis, so continuing clockwise, we then see another `(', so...
    ``signal is a function passing an int and a pointer to a function passing an int returning nothing (void) returning a pointer to a function passing an int returning...
  • Finally we continue and the only thing left is the word `void', so the final complete definition for signal is:
    ``signal is a function passing an int and a pointer to a function passing an int returning nothing (void) returning a pointer to a function passing an int returning nothing (void)''

The same rule is applied for const and volatile. For Example: 

	const char *chptr;
  • Now, what is chptr??
    ``chptr is a pointer to a char constant''

How about this one: 

	char * const chptr;
  • Now, what is chptr??
    ``chptr is a constant pointer to char''

Finally: 

	volatile char * const chptr;
  • Now, what is chptr??
    ``chptr is a constant pointer to a char volatile.''

Practice this rule with the examples found in K&R II on page 122.

[This was posted to comp.lang.c by its author, David Anderson, on 1994-05-06.]

大卫·安德森

有一种称为“顺时针/螺旋规则”的技术，它使任何 C 程序员都可以在头脑中解析任何 C 声明！

需要遵循三个简单的步骤：

  1. 从未知元素开始，沿螺旋/顺时针方向移动；当遇到以下元素时，将其替换为相应的英文语句： [X] 或 [] => Array X size of... 或数组未定义大小... (type1, type2) => 传递 type1 和 type2 的函数返回... * => 指向...的指针 继续以螺旋/顺时针方向执行此操作，直到覆盖所有标记。 始终首先解决括号中的任何问题！

示例#1：简单声明

                     +-------+
                     | +-+   |
                     | ^ |   |
                char *str[10];
                 ^   ^   |   |
                 |   +---+   |
                 +-----------+
Question we ask ourselves: What is str?
``str 是一个...
  • 我们从“str”开始沿顺时针螺旋方向移动，我们看到的第一个字符是“[”，所以，这意味着我们有一个数组，所以...``str是一个数组10...
  • 继续顺时针螺旋方向，接下来我们遇到的是“*”，所以，这意味着我们有指针，所以...``str是一个由10个指针组成的数组...
  • 继续沿螺旋方向前进，我们会看到行尾（“;”），因此继续前进，我们会得到“char”类型，因此...“str 是一个由 10 个指向 char 的指针组成的数组”
  • 我们现在已经“访问”了每个令牌；因此我们完成了！

示例 #2：指向函数声明的指针

                     +--------------------+
                     | +---+              |
                     | |+-+|              |
                     | |^ ||              |
                char *(*fp)( int, float *);
                 ^   ^ ^  ||              |
                 |   | +--+|              |
                 |   +-----+              |
                 +------------------------+
Question we ask ourselves: What is fp?
``fp is a...
  • 顺时针方向螺旋移动，首先看到的是一个‘)’；因此，fp 在括号内，所以我们继续括号内的螺旋，看到的下一个字符是“*”，所以...“fp 是一个指向...的指针”
  • 我们现在走出括号并继续沿顺时针方向螺旋，我们看到“(”；因此，我们有一个函数，所以...“fp是一个指向函数的指针，该函数传递一个int，一个指向float返回的指针...
  • 以螺旋方式继续，然后我们看到“*”字符，所以...“fp 是一个指向函数的指针，该函数传递一个 int 和一个指向 float 的指针，返回一个指向...的指针”
  • 以螺旋方式继续，我们看到“;”，但我们还没有访问所有标记，因此我们继续并最终到达“char”类型，因此...“fp 是一个指向函数的指针，该函数传递一个 int 和一个指向 float 的指针，返回一个指向 char 的指针”

示例#3：“终极”

                      +-----------------------------+
                      |                  +---+      |
                      |  +---+           |+-+|      |
                      |  ^   |           |^ ||      |
                void (*signal(int, void (*fp)(int)))(int);
                 ^    ^      |      ^    ^  ||      |
                 |    +------+      |    +--+|      |
                 |                  +--------+      |
                 +----------------------------------+

我们问自己的问题：什么是“信号”？

请注意，信号位于括号内，因此我们必须首先解决这个问题！

  • 沿顺时针方向移动，我们看到“(”，所以我们有...“信号是一个传递 int 和 a...的函数”
  • 嗯，我们可以在“fp”上使用相同的规则，所以...... 什么是 fp? fp 也在括号内，所以继续我们看到一个“*”，所以...... fp 是一个指向...的指针
  • 继续顺时针螺旋方向，我们到达 `('，所以...``fp 是一个指向传递 int 返回的函数的指针...''
  • 现在我们继续走出函数括号，我们看到 void，所以...``fp 是一个指向传递 int 且不返回任何内容的函数的指针 (void)''
  • 我们已经完成了 fp，所以让我们赶上 `signal'，我们现在......``signal 是一个传递 int 的函数和一个指向传递 int 的函数的指针，不返回任何内容（void）返回...
  • 我们仍然在括号内，所以看到的下一个字符是“*”，所以...“信号是一个传递 int 的函数和一个指向传递 int 的函数的指针，该函数不返回任何内容（void），返回一个指向...的指针”
  • 现在我们已经解决了括号内的项目，所以继续顺时针方向，然后我们看到另一个“(”，所以...“信号是一个传递 int 的函数和一个指向传递 int 的函数的指针，该函数不返回任何内容 (void) 返回一个指向传递 int 返回的函数的指针...
  • 最后我们继续，唯一剩下的就是“void”这个词，所以信号的最终完整定义是：“信号是一个函数，传递一个 int 和一个指向传递 int 不返回任何内容 (void) 的函数的指针，返回一个指向传递 int 不返回任何内容 (void) 的函数的指针”

同样的规则也适用于 const 和 volatile。 例如：

	const char *chptr;
  • 现在，什么是 chptr？ “chptr 是指向 char 常量的指针”

这个怎么样：

	char * const chptr;
  • 现在，什么是 chptr？ “chptr 是指向 char 的常量指针”

最后：

	volatile char * const chptr;
  • 现在，什么是 chptr？ “chptr 是一个指向 char 易失性的常量指针。”

通过第 122 页 K&R II 中的示例来实践此规则。
